supersedes_question_of: M065/M090 reported null core+AC loss for every catalog candidate
model_revision_and_sha256: not_applicable: no maintained-model invocation; the deliverable is a sourced arithmetic bound
exact_build_or_run_commands: none mandated; record any computation script in raw/
question: Can the core + AC winding loss of the candidate chokes be bounded tightly enough to decide the frequency trade, using the core MATERIAL's published loss data and the core geometry?
why: M065 reports a 19.38 W switching saving and M090 an 11.82 W saving. M065's DC copper penalty is +6.75 W and M090's is +3.38 W; core+AC loss is the only remaining term and no catalog datasheet publishes it. A defensible upper bound is enough to decide the frequency move.
focus: For 760801202 (65 kHz case), 760801403 (90 kHz case) and the baseline 760800301: identify the core MATERIAL and geometry from the manufacturer datasheet (core series and size, e.g. T50/T37, Ae, le, Ve, AL). Then source the MATERIAL's core-loss data (manufacturer core-loss curves or Steinmetz parameters) and compute or bound the core loss at the operating flux swing and frequency. Also obtain AC winding resistance versus frequency (skin/proximity) if published. The operating envelope: 15.0 A rms, 23.2719 A peak, 4.2043 A pk-pk ripple, DC bias up to 23.3 A, at 65 kHz and 90 kHz. Report an explicit UPPER bound with its assumptions, not a single optimistic point. If the DC-bias effect on core loss cannot be established from published data, say so and bound with the zero-bias and worst-bias cases.
stop_rule: Do not invent material constants or fit loss to a desired outcome. If neither the material loss data nor the flux swing can be established from primary sources, return UNKNOWN naming the exact missing input. A tight bound, an explicit UNKNOWN and a demonstrated infeasibility are all valid outcomes.
